adjudication_records.issue_text: Test reader thread can spin forever/leak: `deletedAll.set(true)` runs after the delete forEach, so a deletion exception causes the reader loop to hot-loop issuing admin requests indefinitely; use try/finally or fail after N iterations (P3, confidence 50)

adjudication.rationale: In `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti`, the reader thread loops `while (!deletedAll.get())` and the flag is only set via `deletedAll.set(true)` after the delete `forEach`. If any deletion call (`managedRealm.admin().groups().group(groupUuid).remove()`) throws, the test method will exit early and never set the flag, leaving a non-daemon thread hot-looping admin requests indefinitely (and potentially hanging the test run since the thread is never joined/stopped in a `finally`).

Test's catch-Exception-and-continue loop masks intermittent errors as hot retries, producing a pile of unrelated exceptions attributed to the concurrency bug and weakening diagnostic value (P3, confidence 50)

adjudication.rationale: In the new test `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti`, the reader thread runs a tight `while (!deletedAll.get())` loop and catches `Exception` then continues (`caughtExceptions.add(e);`). This can accumulate many exceptions and delay/obscure the first/root failure rather than failing fast, reducing diagnostic value. (It doesn’t truly “mask” errors since the list is asserted empty, but the retry loop can still flood exceptions and weaken the signal.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded full-realm group listing (first=0, max=Integer.MAX_VALUE) issued repeatedly in a tight loop in the test's reader thread, hammering the server and risking CI flakiness/timeouts

This is an unbounded full listing (max = `Integer.MAX_VALUE`) in a tight loop that can hammer the server during CI runs and plausibly cause timeouts/flakiness.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Busy-wait spin loop in reader thread: while (!deletedAll.get()) performs HTTP round trips with no sleep/backoff and no termination guarantee, potentially running forever and leaking HTTP load if setup fails; caughtExceptions also accumulates unboundedly

adjudication.rationale: The new test `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti` starts a reader thread with `while (!deletedAll.get()) { managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(...); }` and no sleep/backoff. The loop only terminates if the main thread reaches `deletedAll.set(true)`, but if group creation/deletion throws before that line, the spawned thread can run indefinitely, continuously issuing HTTP calls. The test also never joins/stops the thread before asserting, and `caughtExceptions` can grow without bound while the loop runs.

The stop flag `deletedAll` is only set after the delete loop; if any exception/error occurs before `deletedAll.set(true)`, the reader thread will spin indefinitely (`while (!deletedAll.get())`), causing a thread leak and potentially hanging the test/JVM. Even on success, lack of join/timeout can leave the thread running past test completion.

adjudication.rationale: In the new test `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti`, a non-daemon reader thread is started with `while (!deletedAll.get()) { ... }`. `deletedAll.set(true)` is only executed after the delete loop. If any `managedRealm.admin().groups().group(groupUuid).remove()` call throws (no try/finally), the test method can abort before setting `deletedAll` to true, leaving the reader thread spinning indefinitely and potentially hanging/leaking a thread in the test JVM.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Test should use an ExecutorService with shutdown, a small sleep, and filter caught exceptions to the expected NPE type

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new concurrency test `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti()` that starts a raw `new Thread(...)` and never joins it or otherwise ensures it has stopped before asserting `caughtExceptions` is empty. It only flips `deletedAll` to true and immediately asserts, so the reader thread may still be running (and could add exceptions after the assertion), and the thread may outlive the test. Using an `ExecutorService` with shutdown/await termination (and optionally a small sleep/yield to ensure the read loop actually runs) would make the test deterministic and avoid leaking background threads. The suggestion to filter exceptions to an expected type is more speculative, but the thread-management concern is grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Test in GroupTest catches only Exception not Throwable, so Errors (e.g., NoClassDefFoundError, StackOverflowError) escape and are silently dropped; additionally the reader thread is never joined so the test can pass without exercising the concurrent read path

adjudication.rationale: In the new test `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti()`, a reader `new Thread(...).start()` is launched and never joined or otherwise synchronized. The main test thread deletes the groups, sets `deletedAll` to `true`, and immediately asserts `caughtExceptions` is empty, so the test can pass even if the reader thread didn’t meaningfully execute the concurrent read loop (or hadn’t yet recorded any failure). Also, the reader thread only catches `Exception`, so `Error` subclasses thrown in that thread would not be added to `caughtExceptions` and would not necessarily fail the test (since they occur off the main test thread).

If it did not override anything, the code would fail to compile immediately, but the diff provides no evidence of such a mismatch.
